result:
The form now saves the browser-computed BMI as a BMI observation, and the server returns its interpretation. Older encounters without that observation fall back to the browser calculation. This is behind PR #3238 (commit `d4857fb`, "Surface BMI reference ranges in the biometrics table"), tracked as ticket O3-4585. I did not run the test suite; this comes from reading the code and the commit diff.

**What the form stores.** The form computes BMI from weight and height into a `computedBodyMassIndex` field. On save, the commit writes it as a new observation using the `bodyMassIndexUuid` concept (`openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/vitals-biometrics-form/exported-vitals-biometrics-form.workspace.tsx`). When creating, it adds the value as a new obs. When editing, it voids the previous BMI obs and adds a new one, but only if weight or height changed. The browser calculation itself is unchanged and lives in `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/vitals-biometrics-form/vitals-biometrics-form.utils.ts` and `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/common/helpers.ts`.

**How the server judges it.** The BMI concept is now fetched with the other biometrics, so its observation carries an interpretation from the backend. The data resource maps it into `bmiRenderInterpretation`, and the biometrics table renders each cell through `NumericObservation` with that interpretation. The same commit adds `bodyMassIndexUuid` to the vitals config schema and surfaces the BMI cell with its reference-range flag.

**How older encounters still show a value.** `useVitalsAndBiometrics` in `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/common/data.resource.ts` uses the stored BMI when present. If there is none, as with encounters saved before this change, it falls back to `calculateBodyMassIndex` on the stored weight and height. That fallback is not flagged against reference ranges, since no interpretation is stored for it.

Ticket O3-4585 comes from Falkon's verified link for PR #3238. I did not find a separate ticket for the form-side persistence, so I am reporting only this one.

  {"ticket": "O3-4585"}
]

explicit null checks (value != null && value !== '') so that 0 is\ntreated as a real recorded value while undefined, null, and empty strings\ncontinue to mean \"no value\".\n\nAffected layers:\n- assessValue: 0 is now evaluated against reference ranges and flagged\n- prepareObsForSubmission: 0-valued obs are created; editing to 0 no\n  longer voids the old obs without creating a replacement\n- data.resource: 0-valued FHIR observations are no longer dropped from\n  the encounter hash table\n- VitalsHeaderItem: 0 displays with its unit instead of \"Not available\"\n- vitals-header.extension: unit symbols render for 0-valued vitals\n- Form workspace: interpretation and range validation run for 0 values\n- Schema: a form with only a 0-valued field passes \"at least one field\"\n- Input utility functions for surgical cache invalidation:\n  - `invalidateVisitHistory()` - Only invalidates visit history table data\n  - `invalidatePatientEncounters()` - Only invalidates encounter data\n  - `invalidateVisitAndEncounterData()` - Combines both for operations affecting both\n  - `useOptimisticVisitMutations()` - Hook for optimistic updates without network requests\n- Fixes the encounter table cache invalidation regex to handle flexible URL parameter order.\n- Updates all visit/encounter operations to use surgical cache targeting:\n  - Visit creation/editing (`visit-form.workspace.tsx`)\n  - Visit deletion/restoration (`useDeleteVisit.hook.tsx`)\n  - Encounter deletion (`encounters-table.component.tsx`)\n  - Form submissions (`form-entry.workspace.tsx`)\n visit dialog (`end-visit-dialog.component.tsx`)\n- Preserves current visit component performance by avoiding unnecessary revalidation.\n- Ensures the `AllEncountersTable` updates correctly after form
